meta_title: Lightweight VS Code Alternative for Mac (Native) | jplus2
meta_description: jplus2 is a native Mac editor, not Electron: no extensions to manage and no telemetry. Compare it with VS Code and see when VS Code is the better pick.
h1: A lightweight VS Code alternative for Mac
lead: Visual Studio Code is a great editor, but it is built on Electron and leans on extensions. jplus2 is a native Mac editor that comes complete instead. This is an honest comparison, including when VS Code is still the better choice.
card_title: A lightweight VS Code alternative for Mac
card_text: A native Mac editor that comes complete, with no extensions to manage, compared honestly with VS Code.

sections.h2: What VS Code is built on
sections.html: VS Code's own FAQ refers to the Electron shell it uses. It collects usage data by default and sends it to Microsoft. You can turn that off with the Telemetry: Telemetry Level setting, although extensions have their own telemetry.

• It is a native Cocoa app, not an Electron app.
  • Features are built in, not extensions: in the full version, IntelliSense, run and debug, SQL, GitHub and an AI assistant.
  • No account and no analytics. API keys and tokens are kept in the macOS Keychain.
  • A small download: the free Lite is about {size}.
  • Light and dark appearance that follow macOS.

sections.h2: When VS Code is the better choice
sections.html:
• You rely on specific extensions or on workflows built around them.
  • You need language support beyond what jplus2 offers: jplus2 gives IntelliSense for C, C++, Objective-C, Swift and Python out of the box, and uses a language server for other languages only if one is installed on your Mac.
  • You also work on Windows or Linux and want the same editor everywhere.

• Quick edits, scripts and small projects where you want an editor that works at first launch.
  • Data work: SQL on CSV and Excel files, Databricks and Snowflake (full version).
  • Privacy-minded work: no account, no analytics, and an AI assistant that can use a local model.
  • A Mac you would rather keep free of a heavy toolchain.

• jplus2 is version 1.0 from a single author, with less mileage than long-established editors.
  • There is no plugin system.
  • The Mac App Store version runs in Apple's sandbox, so Compile and Run use the tools that come with macOS and Xcode.

faq.q: Is jplus2 lighter than VS Code?
faq.a: jplus2 is a native app, and the Lite download is about {size}. We have not published a benchmark against VS Code, so we make no speed claims.

faq.q: Does jplus2 support VS Code extensions?
faq.a: No. jplus2 has no extension system; its features are built in.

faq.q: Can I use my own AI model?
faq.a: Yes, in the full version: Claude with your own API key, any OpenAI-compatible service, or a local model such as Ollama.
Yes. The full version is on the Mac App Store. The free Lite is available now.
